Daily Digest Wednesday, May 27, 2026

Claude Laps OpenAI in Enterprise (Up 128%), Agentic AI's Trust Gap, Adaptive UX Engines Arrive

Anthropic

  1. 1

    Anthropic's Claude Surges 128% in Enterprise While OpenAI Slips 8%

    New Enterprise Technology Research data, reported by The Wall Street Journal, shows Claude's enterprise adoption up 128% over twelve months while OpenAI slipped 8%. Anthropic's ad-free pledge and enterprise-first positioning is paying off — they now hold 34.4% of business adoption share according to the Ramp AI Index.

    Read on LiveNewsChat ↗
  2. 2

    Forbes: Agentic AI Won't Scale Without Enterprise Context

    Forbes Tech Council piece nails the four barriers holding back agentic AI: data fragmentation, process complexity, skills gap, and the trust gap. If an agent makes a decision nobody can explain, it gets ignored. The insight: organizations need a "trust layer" that explains why actions were recommended.

    Read on Forbes ↗
  3. 3

    Adaptive UX Engines: AI That Personalizes Enterprise Software Interfaces

    Most enterprise software frustrates both beginners and power users equally. HyperTrends explores how "Adaptive UX Engines" use AI to personalize interfaces based on user behavior, improving retention and productivity. The implication for PMMs: your product's UX can now learn and adapt per user.

    Read on HyperTrends ↗
  4. 4

    B2B Content in 2026: What to Automate, What to Keep Human

    Vajra Global's practical guide draws the line. AI excels at: trend analysis, outline generation, performance-based suggestions. Keep human: voice, strategic narrative, relationship-building content. The key insight: smaller teams can now compete with larger orgs by strategically automating production work.

    Read on Vajra Global ↗
  5. 5

    Taiwan's III Partners with Skymizer for On-Premise Enterprise AI

    Institute for Information Industry partners with Skymizer to build Taiwan's complete AI infrastructure path — from single edge devices to enterprise on-premise racks to mini data center inference clusters. Signals growing demand for sovereign, on-prem AI options outside the hyperscaler ecosystem. Read this one: The Forbes piece on agentic AI's trust gap. This is the real bottleneck — not capability, but explainability. If your AI agent can't explain itself, humans will override it. For PMMs: positioning AI products needs to address trust, not just automation. That "trust layer" concept is going to matter more than raw performance.
